---
title: "iblatlas"
---

`iblatlas` puts mouse brain anatomy — and the datasets other groups have registered to it — in
**one common reference space**.

That is the whole argument for the package. Two things follow from it:

- **The registration work is already done.** Gene expression, cell types, connectivity and
  cortical depth have each been put into the Allen reference space once, carefully. You join
  them to your own data by a coordinate or an Allen region id, and nothing else.
- **One set of tools works on all of it.** Remapping, the flat maps and the Swanson projection
  operate on any per-region value, so whatever you can already plot for your own recordings you
  can plot for any of these datasets.

::: {.callout-note}
These two are a provisional choice of what to lead with. If a different pair of advantages
would land better with your audience, this is the paragraph to change.
:::

## Read these before you trust your coordinates

Two conventions cause more trouble than everything else combined:

- **[Coordinates and volumes](explanation/coordinates-and-volumes.qmd)** — metres, bregma-relative,
  (ML, AP, DV); deeper is *more negative*; volumes are indexed (AP, ML, DV), not the same order.
- **[Choosing an atlas](explanation/choosing-an-atlas.qmd)** — Allen, Needles and MRI Toronto are
  one volume with different scalings, and they disagree by about 7% in depth.
